# CONFORMANCE

The conformance ID register. Every test name ends in its ID; a test whose
ID is not listed here fails `cargo xtask check-model`, and so does an ID
listed here with no scenario and no test (`CM-02`).

The three honesty levels (R2):

| Level | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `some-true` | A fact reproduced from an authority. **Not established here.** |
| `build` | Constructed here and validated against its oracle. Evidence, not a proof. |
| `open` | Measured and reported. **Never asserted.** |

`cargo xtask audit-limits` fails if a shipped crate returns `Result` over an
error type not registered for it in `model/failures.toml`, if a registered type
is not a closed enum whose variants are exactly its rows, or if the crate does
not forbid `unwrap`, `expect` and `panic!` (R5).

| ID | Level | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EN-01` | `build` | The kernel client writes each request exactly as the kernel examples have it and reads every answer the kernel gives |
| `EN-02` | `build` | A safetensors header is read into its tensors in file order, with every tensor byte range accepted by the kernel |
| `EN-03` | `build` | A model config is read into the preflight question: a named family is recognised, every missing required key is counted, and an unsupported activation is flagged |
| `EN-04` | `build` | An ONNX model's default-domain opset, its nodes' operators in file order and the tensors its graph carries are read from the file, and fields the preflight does not need are stepped over |
| `EN-05` | `build` | The operators an ONNX model names that a builder does not implement are counted into the kernel's import question, and reported each once in the order they first appear |
| `EN-06` | `some-true` | A buffer's label is the BLAKE3 hash of its bytes, as the published test vectors give it |
| `EN-07` | `build` | A download's label and length do not depend on how its bytes were split into chunks |
| `EN-08` | `build` | A download is admitted exactly when the kernel admits the label and length it arrived with against the ones the archive names, and a refusal carries the kernel's verdict |
| `EN-09` | `build` | A conversation takes the step the kernel gives and stays exactly where it was when the kernel refuses |
| `EN-10` | `build` | The trim a conversation proposes drops whole pairs from the oldest, the fewest that leave the rest fitting, and the totals it reports are the totals of those pairs |
| `EN-11` | `build` | A conversation forgets the pairs it proposed only when the kernel accepts the trim, and reads the kernel's bucket and budget as the numbers they are |
| `EN-12` | `build` | Reading an ONNX model costs time in proportion to its nodes: twice the nodes take less than three times as long, and fifty thousand are read in under a second |
| `EN-13` | `build` | Sixteen megabytes of download are labelled at no less than two hundred megabytes a second |
| `EN-14` | `build` | The page asks the kernel what its form says: every field lies where the kernel reads it, every byte of a request is a field of the form it is in, a list is drawn as the groups the kernel indexes into, and every value the examples use can be chosen |
| `EN-15` | `build` | Every reader of a file someone else wrote answers, for any bytes at all: it never panics, it fails only as the register lists, and it answers the same bytes the same way |
| `EN-16` | `build` | A model's tokenizer.json is read only when it is byte-level byte-pair encoding, and a file that describes anything else is refused by what it describes |
| `EN-17` | `build` | Text is encoded by splitting it with the model's own pattern, writing each piece in the byte alphabet, and applying the vocabulary's merges in rank order until none applies |
| `EN-18` | `build` | Decoding what was encoded gives back the text, for any text at all, because every byte has a character and every character of the alphabet has a byte |
| `EN-19` | `build` | A conversation counts a turn with the model own tokeniser, so what the kernel is asked about is the model tokens and not the caller word |
| `EN-20` | `build` | The ids this repository gives are the ids the authority's own tokeniser gives, for the same file and the same text |
| `EN-21` | `build` | A model's own GGUF header is read into a tokeniser, with nothing past the metadata read and a pre-tokeniser name this repository has no cited pattern for refused |
| `EN-22` | `build` | A vocabulary read from a GGUF header gives the same ids as the same vocabulary written as a tokenizer.json, which the authority's own tokeniser checks |
| `EN-23` | `build` | The engine runs in a browser: for the same bytes, the wasm module answers what the crates answer |
| `EN-24` | `build` | A download's root is the sha256 of its bytes as they arrive, and it reproduces the standard's own examples |
| `EN-25` | `build` | A weight container's header is read as the published file is written, and a container this engine cannot follow is refused by name |

| ID | Level | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `KN-05` | `build` | A buffer is admitted exactly when its expected and observed labels are equal and its declared and observed lengths are equal |
| `KN-06` | `build` | A tensor byte range is accepted exactly when it starts at or after the previous tensor end and ends within the file |
| `KN-08` | `build` | The decode bucket is at least what is needed, never above the maximum, and never below the current bucket |
| `KN-09` | `build` | A turn token budget never exceeds the context that remains and never exceeds the request |
| `KN-02` | `build` | A model is supported or derived exactly when no required key is missing, no unsupported feature is flagged and the manifest fits, and only then may weights download |
| `KN-04` | `build` | The quantisation tier chosen fits in memory whenever any tier does, and more memory never lowers it |
| `KN-11` | `build` | A requested dimension is bound exactly when it lies within its bounds, to a size at least the request and never above the upper bound |
| `KN-07` | `build` | A proposed trim is accepted exactly when what remains fits the context and restoring the newest dropped pair would not |
| `KN-03` | `build` | A proposed stage plan is accepted exactly when its stage fits the memory budget, is the largest that does, and its stages cover every layer once |
| `KN-01` | `build` | Each working state is entered from exactly one state by exactly one event, failed is left only by reset, and every other step is refused |
| `KN-10` | `build` | A graph is importable exactly when its opset lies within the implemented window and no operator is unimplemented, and a wider window never makes an importable graph unimportable |
| `KN-12` | `build` | WebGPU is chosen exactly when the adapter is present and the model largest buffer fits its binding limit, and a wider limit never takes WebGPU away |
| `KN-13` | `build` | A weight block length is the one its format and shape imply, and a shape whose columns do not divide into the format groups is refused |
| `KN-14` | `build` | A claimed greedy pick is accepted exactly when its index is the first position holding the maximum score and the claimed score is that maximum |
| `KN-15` | `build` | A token is kept unpenalised exactly when no position inside the recent window holds it |
| `KN-16` | `build` | A speculative commit count is accepted exactly when every draft before the last committed position equals its verified pick and the draft at that position, if any, differs |
| `KN-17` | `build` | Unpacking a packed weight group returns the code packed at each place, for each format, and each code maps to its stated level |

## Cited authorities

Never re-derived, vendored, or gated on.

| Authority | Citation | Evidence here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BLAKE3` | BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3, test_vectors/test_vectors.json at commit ae3e8e6b3a5ae3190ca5d62820789b17886a0038 (2020-09-29), vendored at model/authorities/blake3-test-vectors.json. The algorithm is specified in `BLAKE3: one function, fast everywhere` (O'Connor, Aumasson, Neves, Wilcox-O'Hearn, 2020). | `EN-06` |
| `GGUF` | ggml-org/ggml, docs/gguf.md. The header layout read here is its `gguf_header_t` and `gguf_metadata_kv_t`: the magic `GGUF`, a little-endian version, the tensor and metadata counts, then a key, a value type and a value for each entry. The tokeniser keys are its `tokenizer.ggml.model`, `.pre`, `.tokens`, `.merges` and `.token_type`, whose values are the format's own GGUFTokenType enumeration: 1 normal, 2 unknown, 3 control, 4 user-defined, 5 unused, 6 byte. | `EN-21` |
| `LLAMA-CPP-PRE` | ggml-org/llama.cpp, src/llama-vocab.cpp at blob e90f1bd117d412a3fc9672ddd10c5d12ded0beb2, the `regex_exprs` of LLAMA_VOCAB_PRE_TYPE_GPT2 and LLAMA_VOCAB_PRE_TYPE_QWEN2 and the names mapped to each. A GGUF file carries `tokenizer.ggml.pre` as a name only; the pattern it stands for lives in the reader. | `EN-21`, `EN-22` |
| `SHA-256` | NIST FIPS 180-4, `Secure Hash Standard`, August 2015, Appendix B: the one-block message `abc`, the two-block message `abcdbcde...nopq`, and the message of one million `a`, each with its digest. The implementation is the `sha2` crate, a locked crates.io release (R6). | `EN-24` |
| `HOLK-BONSAI` | HOLOGRAMTECH/q-ternary-bonsai-1.7b on huggingface.co at revision c6d6a12384ecc52ae7e006bef263bfedf5e7496c, the file q-ternary-bonsai-1.7b.v1.holo, bytes 0 to 98,313, vendored at model/authorities/holk-bonsai-header.bin. The file itself is 424,013,749 bytes and is not vendored; these are the bytes a reader has to get right before it can ask for any of the rest. | `EN-25` |
